v.why: Replacing none adds a whole path to the output, while replacing a skip only swaps an already useful identity path.
The skip already carries signal to the output, so the conv's marginal gain is smaller.
Going from no edge to a conv adds a new route and so gains more than swapping existing ops.
Pooling is a weak incumbent on the input edge, so replacing it with a conv gains more than replacing a skip.
Adding a direct conv path where none existed gains more than overwriting skip or pool.
A skip on the 1->2 edge already passes features, leaving less to gain from a conv.
A 3x3 conv upstream already supplies the receptive field, so the downstream conv shows diminishing returns.
With edge 1 removed node 2 is fed only through edge 2, so a conv on edge 5 operates on weaker features.
Removing edge 0 starves node 1 and the 0->1->2->3 chain, so a conv on edge 5 has less to process.
With edge 0 absent node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 4 is nearly wasted.
An upstream 3x3 conv already supplies spatial mixing, making a downstream 1x1 conv partially redundant.
The direct skip already provides an identity route to the output, making a conv route less valuable.
A skip on edge 3 reduces what an extra conv on edge 4 contributes at node 3.
A skip on the direct edge makes the deeper 0->2->3 conv route less necessary.
The identity shortcut at node 3 weakens the marginal benefit of enriching the 1->2 path.
Without a direct edge the network depends on conv paths through nodes 1 and 2, so adding capacity matters more.
A conv route into node 3 already exists, so adding the identity shortcut yields less.
A conv on edge 5 already supplies strong features at node 3, reducing the marginal value of a shortcut.
Pooling into node 2 blurs its input, and a conv on edge 5 can recover discriminative features.
A conv on the sibling edge into node 2 compensates for the weak pooled branch.
With a pooled sibling at node 3, the conv on edge 5 becomes the main feature-extracting route.
A pooled edge 5 leaves node 3 under-powered, so a conv on edge 4 contributes more.
The two convs feeding node 2 act as substitutes, so a second conv gains less.
A conv on edge 4 already enriches node 3, making an additional 1x1 conv on edge 5 partly redundant.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is dead, so a conv on edge 1->2 has no signal to transform.
A dead node 1 makes any op on edge 4 nearly irrelevant, so the edit's effect collapses.
Creating the direct 0->3 conv path adds a short high-capacity route that is worth more than upgrading an existing op.
Restoring a missing input branch to node 2 gains more than upgrading an existing op.
Node 2 already receives an identity path from the input, so a conv adds less than when replacing a weaker op.
When edge 1 is absent, edge 2 is the only feed into node 2, so making it a conv matters more.

I dropped six hypotheses: the four skip-connect edits (restoring sharpness after a pool, offsetting smoothing), which rest on speculative mechanisms and have small effects. I also dropped the edge 2 skip edit conditioned on an edge 1 pool, which was low-capacity reasoning with no clear margin, and the edge 4 skip edit conditioned on an edge 0 pool. I replaced them with structural-connectivity hypotheses, such as dead-node effects and none-versus-skip replacement, where the interaction should be large and consistent across datasets.
